history.period: Construction begun c. 1810 by Appasaheb Patwardhan; idol consecrated 1843 by Thorle (elder) Chintamanrao Patwardhan; mandap completed 1952
history.summary: The Shri Ganapati Mandir of Sangli is the most famous Ganapati temple in southern Maharashtra, on the eastern bank of the Krishna river in Sangli city. It is the kuldaivat (tutelary deity) of the Patwardhan sardars of Sangli — and, by popular belief, of more than half the population of Sangli — who owed their rise to this deity's blessings. Construction was started by the late Appasaheb Patwardhan and took over 30 years; the idol was installed in 1843 by Thorle Chintamanrao Patwardhan. The temple is built of black stone brought from the Jyotiba hills near Kolhapur, hauled on huge platforms pulled by teams of about fifteen bullocks. It stands in a large quadrangular court over about two acres, with sanctum, middle chamber, outer chamber (sabha-griha) and Nagarkhana. The idol is of white marble on a golden throne, about 45 cm high, with Riddhi and Siddhi on either side; devotees regard it as swayambhu (self-manifested). The main doors are carved from different-coloured natural wood, and the idol is positioned so it is visible from any part of Ganapati Peth. The complex is a Ganapati panchayatana with four corner shrines to Umarameshwar (Shankar), Suryanarayana, Chintamaneshwari and Lakshminarayan (Vishnu), plus a Navagraha temple and a statue of Chintamanrao Patwardhan. The mandap was added later and completed in 1952, inaugurated by Vice-President Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. It is also called 'Ganeshdurg' because during the freedom struggle its premises served as a meeting point for Lokmanya Tilak and Mahatma Gandhi. Identity note: of the several Ganapati shrines in Sangli-Miraj, this Patwardhan temple in Ganapati Peth, Sangli city, is the most likely referent of the generic CSV row 'Ganapati Temple, Sangli'.

name: Ganapati Temple, Sangli (Shri Ganapati Mandir)
town_description: Sangli is a major city in western Maharashtra on the eastern bank of the Krishna river, known for its sugarcane, turmeric and grape trade; the historic Ganapati temple stands in Ganapati Peth in the old city on the Krishna bank.

travel.airport: Kolhapur Airport (~55 km); Pune Airport (~230 km)
travel.road: Sangli is on NH-48 (Mumbai-Bengaluru highway) and well connected by MSRTC and private buses

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Ganesh Chaturthi is the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official visiting hours not published - verify locally before visiting
